newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Late South African bonds edged weaker after U.S. Treasury yields soared to three month highs following stronger-than-expected job creation data but bond traders said reaction was muted.

They said the local bond market was swept by bullish sentiment and had tended to overlook the bearish U.S. employment report, focusing instead on improved money market rates, a positive technical outlook and expectations of a bullish budget in March.
At 1418 GMT the benchmark R150 stock was trading at 15.795 percent from 15.90 percent late on Thursday.
Traders expected further strength at the start of next week with 15.72 percent the immediate level to break on the downside and 15.45 percent targeted over the next month.
"The market is in a bull phase and has tended to ignore the U.S. data," a trader at a major South African bank said, adding that most players expected more strength next week.
"There was some local buying on the day but most of the support came from offshore players covering positions," another dealer said.
Some bond traders pointed out that the size of positions taken in the market was not that big as the holiday season was still a factor.
Dealers and bankers said a rash of Eurorand bond issues, which saw a further 350 million rand hit the market via two new issues on Friday, had also heartened the local South African bond market.
But they said demand for the new wave of rand paper was being driven primarily by a desire among existing investors to roll over their losses rather than any new confidence in South African debt.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net sellers of 59.38 million rand of South African bonds on Thursday from a net buying position of 217.44 million rand on Wednesday.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 34.90 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement date -- from 4.12 billion rand on Wednesday, the exchange said.
On the currency market the rand ended a choppy day weaker on the dollar in trade characterised by good two-way business, forex traders said.
It closed at 4.6740/6790 on the dollar from 4.6670/6720 on Thursday. Dealers said the 4.6550 level had been difficult to break on the bottom side.
"There was good import business at around the 4.6550 area," a forex trader said, adding that he expected the currency market to take its cue from the bond market at the Monday start.
Another trader said there was potential for the rand to strengthen in the near term
"People are looking more at the technical picture which is looking positive."
Against the crosses, the rand was last trading slightly better at 7.8564/8695 on sterling from 7.9002/9110 late on Thursday and at 0.3371/3376 on the mark from 0.3368/3374 previously.
On the money market, the daily money market shortage fell further to 8.732 billion rand on Thursday from 9.444 billion rand on Wednesday, the Reserve Bank said.

Three-month NCD rates were lower at between 17.30 and 17.60 percent from 17.35 and 17.65 percent, while the 90-day BA rate also fell slightly to between 16.65 and 16.90 percent from 16.65 and 16.95 percent.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
